# Seedance 2.5 Prompt Engine — edit your real footage with AI

> A free, step-by-step guide by Natalia Le (AI Test Tube) to editing real video with Seedance 2.5: swap the outfit or the background while keeping the person's face, hair, body, movement, timing and the original camera. It explains what you need, the rule behind a good edit prompt, a simple free prompt template, and an optional paid tool (the Prompt Engine) that writes a detailed prompt for you in ChatGPT or Claude.

## Pages

- [Guide (English)](https://ai-edit-lab.pages.dev/): the full guide in English.
- [Инструкция (Russian)](https://ai-edit-lab.pages.dev/ru): the same guide in Russian.
- [Prompt Engine on Gumroad](https://aitesttube.gumroad.com/l/pdwsxr): the paid PDF instruction file ($7) plus an examples PDF.

## Key facts

- What you can change: the outfit, the location/background, scene details (add or remove objects, glasses, jewelry, a watch, a bag), light and mood (time of day, weather, studio lighting), and the camera angle or movement only when asked.
- What you need: a source video of 4 to 30 seconds where the person is clearly visible (close-up or full body), one or more reference photos (outfit, location or overall look), and access to Seedance 2.5 (the author uses Segmind; as a rough guide, 30 seconds of 720p there costs about $7, and platform prices change). ChatGPT or Claude is optional.
- The main rule: every Seedance edit prompt has two parts — CHANGE (only what you asked for) and KEEP (face, hair, body and proportions, hands, movement and gestures, facial expressions, composition, camera, timing). If the prompt does not say what to keep, Seedance may change the face, the movement and the camera too.
- File roles: @Video1 is the source video; @Image1 is the first uploaded reference photo, @Image2 the second. The person in a reference photo must not replace the person in the video — the prompt has to say so explicitly ("Do not copy the person from @Image1").
- Write Seedance prompts in English and describe things concretely (color, fabric, cut, place, light); words like "beautiful" or "cinematic" are not instructions.
- A generated reference works well: screenshot a frame from the video, ask an image model (for example ChatGPT Images or Nano Banana) to change the outfit or background, and use that image as the reference — the pose, angle and composition already match.

## The 3-step workflow

1. Get the video and the reference photo ready.
2. Write the prompt. Option A (free): fill in a simple English template — roles of @Video1 and @Image1, "Change only", "Details", and fixed lines that keep the person and the camera. Option B (Prompt Engine): in ChatGPT or Claude, upload the Prompt Engine PDF, then the reference photo, then a screenshot of a video frame, and send the request from the guide; you get a detailed English prompt plus a short explanation in your language.
3. In Seedance 2.5, upload the source video and the reference photos in the same order as in the prompt, paste the prompt and generate. The Prompt Engine file and the screenshot never go into Seedance.

## If the result is off

- The face or movement changed: check that the prompt says what to keep.
- The outfit or location does not match: describe it in more detail.
- Too much changed: change one thing at a time — first the outfit, then the location.

## About the Prompt Engine

A PDF instruction file for ChatGPT or Claude. It reads your frame and reference and builds a structured Seedance 2.5 prompt from up to 12 blocks (files and roles, editing task, outfit, environment, natural motion, lighting, character preservation, motion, camera, integration, critical rules, quality), using only the blocks the edit needs. It is useful for complex scenes — several people, a new location, moving water — where details are easy to miss. The prompt it writes works with Seedance 2.5 on any platform.
